GRU4Rec’s original research supports comparing cross-entropy with BPR-max under expanded negative coverage. BPR-max uses softmax-weighted negatives inside a negative-log pairwise probability, plus score regularization; it differs from averaging weighted BPR losses. The official implementation supports uniform-to-popularity sampling through q(i) ∝ frequency(i)^α. Negative count, sampling distribution, and loss should therefore be separate experimental factors. [GRU4Rec implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec), [original formulation](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18_slides.pdf).

Recent work identifies distinct mechanisms. WWW 2023 connects hard-negative BPR to partial AUC and recommends controllable hardness. UFNRec (SDM 2023) highlights that sampled negatives can represent unobserved interests; its label reversal requires stabilization, so high scores alone do not establish false negatives. A 2024 sequential-recommendation study finds sampling effects vary across datasets and popularity bands. RecSys 2025 revisits logQ correction: the guaranteed positive must be treated differently from sampled denominator items; its evidence concerns retrieval models, not a demonstrated GRU4Rec improvement. [Hard-negative theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.03472), [UFNRec](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/1.9781611977653.ch6), [sampling comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), [logQ correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331).

Experimental implication: first compare sampled softmax and correctly implemented BPR-max using identical negative pools and counts; then vary uniform versus tempered-popularity sampling, correction, and temperature/score regularization separately. Exclude known training positives without consulting held-out labels. On common diagnostic samples, measure margins, negative-score concentration, embedding norms, and popularity bands; these can distinguish coverage and scale effects but cannot identify latent false negatives. Preserve one GRU4Rec model per category and select solely through pinned macro validation HR@10.
